title: Indian-Origin Neel Patel Named in Australia U-19 Squad for Multi-Format Tour of India
excerpt: The NSW opener, who scored over 1,000 runs in Sydney First Grade cricket at 16, joins a 16-member squad for three ODIs and two four-day matches in Rajkot and Ahmedabad next month.
body:
• Indian-origin teenager Neel Patel, a top-order batter and off-spinner from NSW, has been named in Australia's 16-member U-19 squad for a multi-format tour of India in September.
  • The tour includes three 50-over matches and two four-day matches to be played in Rajkot and Ahmedabad.
  • Patel became one of the youngest players to score more than 1,000 runs in Sydney Premier Cricket First Grade in a calendar year at the age of 16.
  • Will Byrom and Kasey Barton are the only two squad members with U-19 World Cup experience from the 2026 tournament in Zimbabwe.

Indian-origin cricketer Neel Patel has been selected in Australia's Under-19 men's squad for a multi-format tour of India next month, Cricket Australia announced on Sunday. The 16-member squad will play three 50-over matches and two four-day matches against India's U-19 side in Rajkot and Ahmedabad.

Patel, a top-order right-hand batter who also bowls off-spin, represents the University of New South Wales (UNSW) Cricket Club in Sydney Premier Cricket. He became one of the youngest players to amass more than 1,000 runs in First Grade in a calendar year at the age of 16, according to IANS.

A Meticulous Approach to the Game

Patel's rise through Australian youth cricket has been marked by an unusually disciplined approach for a teenager. He maintains a OneNote file that tracks his performances after every match, recording what he did well and where he can improve.

https://x.com/toisports/status/2084107189355171999

"The OneNote keeps track of my performances; what I did well and what I can improve on for every single game, so I'm always learning."

— Neel Patel, speaking to cricket.com.au

At a recent talent camp in Adelaide as part of Cricket Australia's 2028 U-19 World Cup development cycle, Patel revealed he has been focused on improving his back-foot play. "Batting wise, it's back-foot stuff. I've been given advice from my coaches on how to work on that," he told cricket.com.au. "Then also fielding, and the strength and fitness side of the game."

Away from the field, the teenager enjoys cooking, playing chess with his dad, and building LEGO sets.

Squad Composition and World Cup Experience

Fast bowlers Will Byrom and Kasey Barton will spearhead the bowling attack and are the only two members of the squad who featured at the U-19 World Cup in Zimbabwe earlier this year. Byrom starred in that tournament with 10 wickets at an average of 10.50, while Barton contributed four wickets before Australia's run ended with a 27-run semi-final loss to England.

The full squad includes Kasey Barton, Hayden Barbulovi, Eli Brain, Will Byrom, Blake Cattle, Jack Czosnek, Spencer Green, Connor Gregory, Charlie Henderson, Zed Hollick, Matthew Lough, Neel Patel, Jacob Pietz, Patrick Sullivan, Theo Tsingos, and Thomas Vaseo.

"We are really pleased to provide the opportunity to some of Australia's best young players to continue their development as part of our pathways program. Touring India and playing against high-quality opposition in challenging conditions will be a valuable experience and test the players technically and mentally across formats."

— Sonya Thompson, Cricket Australia Head of National Development

Diaspora Connections on Both Sides

Patel follows a growing tradition of Indian-origin players representing Australia at the youth level. In the 2026 U-19 World Cup squad, Aryan Sharma and John James were of Indian heritage, while Nitesh Samuel and Naden Cooray traced their roots to Sri Lanka. The presence of players of South Asian descent in Australian cricket's pathway programs reflects the deepening imprint of the subcontinent's diaspora communities in Australian sport.

For Patel, touring India will carry a personal dimension. Playing on pitches tailored for spin — his secondary skill — against the country of his heritage adds a layer of significance that statistics alone cannot capture.

What's Next

The India tour is part of Cricket Australia's broader player development strategy ahead of the 2028 U-19 World Cup cycle. Separately, a CA Development squad has landed in Chennai for the annual MRF Academy Program, which will feature two multi-day matches on spin-friendly pitches scheduled for August 5–6 and August 10–11.

The U-19 series against India is expected to begin in September, with full schedules and broadcast details to be confirmed by Cricket Australia.
